# Tool installation audit

<!-- Generated by python/generate_install_audit.py from config/tool_installers.tsv, config/metagenomic_tool_installers.tsv and config/source_tools.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

What happens when a tool is enabled and a run, `plasbench check --yes`, `plasbench install-tools` or the window needs it, per tool. Revisions are 40-character commit
SHAs resolved from the release tag on the date shown; a tag or branch name is never what is fetched. Times are estimates unless stated: nothing here was timed on a
real conda solve. The *CI proof* column is what `.github/workflows/tool-install-proof.yml` showed on a clean Linux runner (config/install_proof_result.json).

## How installation works now

| Situation | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `plasbench install-tools PROFILE --yes` | Installs the profile. A source-built tool shows its plan (repository, pinned commit, size, licence) first and needs `--yes` (or `y` at a terminal): without it nothing changes and the exit code is 21. |
| `plasbench install-tools a,b,c --yes` | Several profiles in one command (the window's *Install all enabled tools*). |
| Exit 20 | A tool that cannot be installed automatically (verified reason and recipe printed). Information, not a failure: no `ERROR`, not red, in the console, the terminal page, the window state and `scripts/lib.sh`. |
| `plasbench run` / `check` with an enabled tool missing | Stage 0 lists every missing tool. At a terminal it asks; with `--yes`, `INSTALL_MISSING_TOOLS=1` or `plasbench run --install-missing-tools` it installs first and checks again in the same process (it no longer asks you to open a new shell); with no terminal and no consent it stops before any sample work, naming every missing tool and the exact command. |
| Stage 4 reached with a tool still missing | One notice names every missing enabled tool; each is recorded as `skipped` with the reason `command unavailable (not installed; run: plasbench install-tools PROFILE --yes)`, never silently dropped. |
| The window | *Install* / *Update* per tool on the Tools page and Workflow cards, *Install all enabled tools* (one consent dialog), a progress strip, and an offer to install missing enabled tools before a run starts. Tools are marked stale after an install so the next probe re-checks. |
| Isolation and safety | Each source-built tool gets its own environment next to the main one; the clone is staged and moved; a failure removes everything it created and restores a previous working install; https only; no sudo; no piped shell installers. |

## Tools that cannot be installed automatically, with the evidence

### plsmd

Upstream distributes only a Dockerfile, not a release. The Dockerfile downloads 'Miniconda3-latest' and unpinned conda packages when it builds, so two builds of the same commit are not the same image; the repository's only tag (v1.0) predates the Dockerfile (labelled v1.2); there is no licence file; and running it needs a Docker daemon, whose installation needs administrator rights that PlasBench never uses.

Evidence (fetched 2026-11-19):
- https://github.com/Genomics-and-Metagenomics-Unit-57357/plsMD/blob/9cbff566cdad115b8dd5801ea53ff75092aaeaf7/Dockerfile
- https://api.github.com/repos/Genomics-and-Metagenomics-Unit-57357/plsMD/tags
- https://github.com/Genomics-and-Metagenomics-Unit-57357/plsMD/blob/9cbff566cdad115b8dd5801ea53ff75092aaeaf7/README.md

Recipe:
1. Install Docker yourself (needs administrator rights) and make sure `docker info` works.
2. git clone https://github.com/Genomics-and-Metagenomics-Unit-57357/plsMD.git && cd plsMD && git checkout 9cbff566cdad115b8dd5801ea53ff75092aaeaf7 && git rev-parse HEAD   (must print that 40-character revision)
3. docker build -t plsmd .   (add --build-arg DOWNLOAD_DB=true to fetch PLSDB during the build)
4. Record the image digest in your study notes: docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' plsmd
5. Put plsMD_wrapper.sh on PATH as `plsMD` (or set PLSMD_CMD), set PLSMD_DB to your PLSDB BLAST index, then run `plasbench check`.

### ppr-meta

PPR-Meta's executable needs the MATLAB Runtime R2018a (v94), which MathWorks distributes only after a click-through licence on mathworks.com, so it cannot be fetched on your behalf; the Python side is Python 2.7 with TensorFlow 1.4.1 and Keras 2.0.8, all end of life, with no maintained conda package; the repository has no release that fixes these versions.

Evidence (fetched 2026-11-19):
- https://github.com/zhenchengfang/PPR-Meta/blob/ab99c9102acdcf331c169900a60f1bdaa92aaeaa/README.md
- https://api.anaconda.org/package/bioconda/ppr-meta
- https://www.mathworks.com/products/compiler/matlab-runtime.html

Recipe:
1. Install the MATLAB Runtime R2018a (v94) from https://www.mathworks.com/products/compiler/matlab-runtime.html (accept MathWorks' licence) and add its runtime/bin/sys/extern directories to LD_LIBRARY_PATH as the PPR-Meta README says.
2. Create a Python 2.7 environment with numpy, h5py, tensorflow==1.4.1 and keras==2.0.8 (README, 'Installation').
3. git clone https://github.com/zhenchengfang/PPR-Meta.git && cd PPR-Meta && git checkout ab99c9102acdcf331c169900a60f1bdaa92aaeaa && git rev-parse HEAD   (must print that 40-character revision)
4. Run PPR_Meta on your contigs, then: plasbench normalize-meta-classifier --tool ppr_meta --input result.csv --out tool/community.classification.tsv

## Inputs the runtime does not include

- **gplas2**: gplas2_mob needs MOB-suite output (mob_recon profile); gplas2_external needs per-sample classifier tables you provide (--gplas2-external-predictions-dir)
- **plasme**: The PLASMe database (about 12.4 GB): installed by `plasbench check --yes` (env/download_plasme_db.sh).
- **plasgraph2**: The pretrained model ships inside the checkout; PlasBench points PLASGRAPH2_MODEL_DIR at <install>/plasbench-src/model/ESKAPEE_model when you have not set it.
- **plasmidec**: plasmidEC.sh builds its own conda environments (plasmidEC_R, plasmidEC_centrifuge, plasmidEC_platon, plasmidEC_rfplasmid) and downloads the Centrifuge and Platon databases from Zenodo the first time it runs (about 20 minutes, internet needed). That step belongs to the tool and is not pinned by PlasBench.
- **plasbin_flow**: A Gurobi licence (free for academics, from gurobi.com): the pip package gurobipy runs only size-limited models without one. PlasBench cannot obtain a licence for you.
- **plasbin_flow**: A gzipped GFA with dp or KC tags, a plasmid-score file and a GC-probability file (PlasBench adapts the output; it does not run PlasBin-flow itself).
- **mobilome-map**: A container engine (Docker, Singularity or Apptainer) is needed when the pipeline runs: installing one needs administrator rights, which PlasBench never uses. The pipeline downloads its own container images and Nextflow plugins on its first run.
- **plsmd**: A PLSDB BLAST index (PLSMD_DB) and a Unicycler assembly.
